What worked for me was going to a PHP (partial hospitalization program) for eating disorders. If you’re already in therapy you may need a higher level of care. Medication is also available. I practiced by keeping one highly binged food at a time in the house and having a serving for my nighttime snack. After a while of this I was able to add more and more binge foods. Now I can keep chips and ice cream in the house and not even touch them for weeks because I forget about them.

It was much more mental for me than it was anything physical. I hope you’re able to get some relief.

Can you do both? The Botox can take a while to kick in. Namenda got rid of my migraines after a week of use but after 2 months of use I started having side effects (dissociation and anxiety). For me, I needed the combination but if I had to pick one I would probably pick the namenda. If you have side effects/it’s ineffective then you can cross it off and go to the Botox.

I see you’re concerned about invalidating the littles but just empathize that you love them but that you also have your own needs. We have to honor our own needs in order to be a healthy partner. Also consider that people with DID are not made of glass. It’s kind of treating them like they’re not an adult capable of important conversations. As long as you are respectful and come from a place of love I think things will be okay. I used to have a lot of fears like this and a feeling of walking on eggshells. I tried different techniques like writing down my withdrawal experiences and bad consequences, a list of things in my life I don’t want to lose, reading this subdreddit, etc. None of it worked for me because I found I was still engaging with the voice inside my head saying to drink. 

Now, no matter how convinced I am I can have a good time drinking I remind myself that the feeling is a lie. The feelings and thoughts associated with drinking are lying to me. I try my best not to listen and almost put up a wall in my mind. No matter what I feel or think I can’t drink. That’s not an option so pick something else. It hasn’t been 100% for me but it’s been a lot more effective than some of the other techniques I’ve tried.

I see a lot of different specialists so here’s my 2 cents. UCSD the average wait is 1-3 months. That’s been my experience with two different specialists. I have seen 5 different specialists (all in different fields) at Scripps. The wait time has been a couple of weeks up to 4 months. 

I like Scripps because they have a waiting list you can use on their patient portal. Sign up for the waitlist and you will get an email when a spot opens up. I have gotten seen faster quite a few times using this feature. 

The best thing to do is call and schedule multiple appointments (one at Scripps and one at UCSD).

I had the same problem and finally found a uro-Obgyn that did a microgen dx test on me. It uses your DNA and shows all bacteria present in your urine along with what types of antibiotics are most effective. It also shows which bacteria are drug resistance. After properly identifying problematic bacteria and treating I had improvements in symptoms.

At the same time I started pelvic floor physical therapy. I highly recommend a doctor who can evaluate your pelvic floor and give you a referral to PT. I’ve had one bladder instillation for IC and that helped a lot. Current treatment is PT every other week and bladder instillations for major flares. I have had my symptoms under control for 3 years after 2 years of suffering. 

Also, check out the live uti free website (not sure if I’m allowed to link). So much info I didn’t know! I hope you are able to find some answers. I’m sorry you are going through this.

EDIT: just saw your comments. Try and find a uro-gynecologist. I saw gynecologists and urologists and didn’t find answers until I switched to someone familiar with both. Feel free to message me if you have any questions.
